notes:
Company background: mid-stage startup building GitHub-style PR review assistant that summarizes diffs, generates inline comments, ranks suggested reviewers and comments. Product shipped as VSCode extension + GitHub App.

Primary ask: low-latency streaming for live IDE copilots (aim < 80ms chunk latency), model/version pinning per customer, and reranking of generated comments (precision > 0.85 on our eval).

POC: 2-week POC using their internal large-repo dataset (15k PRs). Testing throughput: target 100 QPS for batch generation, peak 500 QPS on canary. Using 8k+ token windows for long diffs; strong interest in KV cache + prefix caching.

Model preferences: prefer smaller open models for dev flow (llama/neoX variants) for price, but want a high-quality fallback (redwood-verified top-tier). Need deterministic pinning and rollback.

Security: SSO + audit logs mandatory for enterprise customers; EU customers require data residency and optional on-prem for high-risk accounts.

Integration needs: GitHub webhook signature verification, GitHub App auth, Drive/Slack connectors for comment sync.

Notes from 2026-03-03 call (Fireflies): SE demoed streaming perf with dedicated pool; customer reiterated P99 under 300ms for 95% of calls, not just median. Ivan (CTO) quote: "We can't ship a copilot that stalls in review flow."

Legal/compliance: sent security FAQ + SOC2 attestation (drive link). Legal requested SLA language and EULA redlines; Redwood legal has started review.

POC blockers: internal benchmark shows 6-8% quality drop when we quantize to 4-bit on long-context; team requests recommended quantization profiles and fallback routing.

Next milestones: run end-to-end POC with dedicated pool + canary routing by 2026-03-15; collect eval metrics (precision/recall on comment relevance) and finalize pricing.

Short-term asks: sample quantization profiles, batching guidance, example rollout policy for model fallback.
